title: Engineering mosaic weekly snapshot — Apr 04 2027
content:
Topline summary:

This is a concise snapshot from the cross-team all-hands held 2027-04-04 (platform + serving + observability). Focus: triage followups from the April 1 latency spike, canary rollout plan for v0.11.2 of the batching runtime, and a short primer on the new cost telemetry dashboard. Mostly operational notes, a few decisions, and action items.

1) Incident followup: April 1 latency spike
- Short recap: a region-level autoscaling misalignment produced sustained high queue depth for 3 hours (SLO breaches on p50/p95 for a subset of high-seq-length customers).
- Root cause (current working hypothesis): a coordination bug between the autoscaler and the scheduler's token-based shard assignments — under rare churn the scheduler dropped a replication spec causing one pool to be undersized.
- Evidence: metrics linked (see JIRA-OPS-987) + flamegraphs from 2027-04-01 03:10-06:45 UTC.
- Immediate mitigations applied: manual pool re-provisioning and temporary bump to min replicas for the affected capacity tier.
- Decision: revert the autoscaler heuristic change rolled out Mar 29; leave the higher min-replica override in place until fixed.
- Owner for fix: Marcus Li. ETA for patch + unit tests: 2027-04-08.

2) Canary rollout: batching runtime v0.11.2 (ops-managed)
- What's in the release: improved KV cache eviction logic, micro-optimizations to attention kernels, and a new safety timeout to avoid unbounded batching groups.
- Canary plan: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 5 days, with hard rollback criteria (p95 latency increase >5% or error increase >0.5% above baseline).
- Observability hooks: new canary dashboard shows per-model p50/p95/p99, queue depth distribution, and batching efficacy (tokens/batch). Link: confluence PLT-1246.
- Rollout owner: Elena Torres. Start date: 2027-04-06.

3) Cost telemetry primer & quick wins
- New cost dashboard (Optimize team) aggregates token-level cost per model variant and per-route. Early insights: small models with high request rate account for ~18% of token cost due to low batchability (high tail latency requests).
- Quick action: add a low-latency async path for short requests (<=128 tokens) to increase batching density; prototype ticket created (ENG-CT-233).
- Owner: Devon Park to spin up prototype; prototype to be demoed 2027-04-12.

4) Rollouts & policy changes
- Canary policy tweak: add automatic snapshot of KV cache on canary launch to enable faster warm-start in case of rollback. This was approved.
- New routing policy: for enterprise-tier customers flagged with SLA-sticky routing, requests may skip a deep-quantized variant when latency-sensitive. Product/PS signoff pending — product owner Sanjay Patel to confirm by 2027-04-09.

5) Developer experience / console notes
- Console: token breakdown now supports a per-route hot-spot heatmap. Early feedback: console perf around heavy queries needs pagination fixes. UX bug filed (GH #3168).
- Docs: short how-to for canary dashboards drafted by Priya; needs review.

6) People & hiring
- Two new SRE hires accepted offers, start dates 2027-04-18 and 2027-05-03. They will be onboarded onto the autoscale and runtime on-call rotations.
- Reminder: sign up for the cross-team shadowing days happening week of 2027-04-19 (email invite sent).

7) Open questions / parking lot
- Do we keep the higher min-replica override as permanent for bursty tenants? Pros/cons discussed; decision deferred to next sync.
- How aggressive should we be with quantized fallbacks for enterprise SLAs vs. cost targets? Product + legal to weigh in.

8) Q&A highlights (from live chat)
- Q: How will fallbacks affect customer metrics? A: fallback will be logged and surfaced in per-customer cost/quality dashboards; a fallback event will also trigger an alert if repeated.
- Q: Are we planning more deterministic scheduling for hotspots? A: exploring bucketed token-length queues as a follow-up.

Action items (short list):
- Marcus Li: Merge autoscaler coordination patch + unit tests (JIRA-OPS-987). Due 2027-04-08.
- Elena Torres: Start v0.11.2 canary (1% traffic) on 2027-04-06; watch canary dashboard every 2 hours during ramp.
- Devon Park: Prototype async low-latency path for <=128 token requests. Demo 2027-04-12.
- Priya Desai: Finish canary dashboard how-to and ping docs review by 2027-04-09.
- Sanjay Patel: Product signoff for SLA routing policy by 2027-04-09.

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Consider short-lived pre-warmed containers for very low-latency slices (might trade cost for predictability) — spike this after async prototype.
- Add regression tests that simulate autoscaler churn with mock scheduler — this would have caught the Mar 29 heuristic change.

Appendix: useful links and artifacts
- Incident board: JIRA-OPS-987
- Canary dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/canary/v0112
- Cost telemetry deck: confluence PLT-1246 (link above)
- Runtime PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124

End of snapshot. If you want me to expand any section into a separate playbook (e.g., canary rollback runbook or autoscaler chaos test plan) I can draft in the next doc.
